correctness.rationale: In characteristic two the three commuting g_i-1 square to zero, generate the group ring, and the squarefree quotient has the same dimension eight. Its positive-degree ideal J is nilpotent and every element with nonzero constant coefficient is a unit. Frobenius gives f²=0 for every f∈J; nevertheless the graph deletes diagonal loops. For f=v+w+txyz and g=v'+w'+t'xyz, the separate degree-two and degree-three product tests are v∧v'=0 and <v,w'>+<v',w>=0. The latter is the perfect pairing in complementary coordinate bases, and the former is exactly proportionality. For nonzero v=αu in a normalized projective direction, equal s=<u,w>/α is precisely the test within that point, and there are (q-1)q²q choices at fixed point and s. For v=0,w≠0, the direction of w defines the projective line and gives q(q-1) possibilities; those vertices annihilate one another. The nonzero degree-three vertices are universal. The cross test is the stated projective incidence, hence precisely a+mb+mqc=q⁷-1 vertices. Internal zero-sum clique vectors give -1, while zero-sum constants across the q separate cliques of a point give c-1. The centered line and point subspaces are preserved by N and Nᵀ since their row and column sums are q+1. On those spaces NNᵀ=qI, so each paired mode gives the displayed quadratic with coupling product bq²c. Uniform line and point coordinates and the universal coordinate give T; the sum of the dimensions is q⁷-1, including a=1 at q=2. At λ=0 the quadratic is 1-c-bq²c<0 and c-1>0. The verified determinant expansion is strictly negative for q≥2 because (q-1)³≥1 and q⁷≥2q⁴. This proves nonsingularity over the reals, not for an adjacency retaining square-zero loops.

evidence: Mönius gives annihilator compression and weighted adjacency machinery; exact rank/nullity Theorems 4.1 and 4.3 assume products of residue-class rings. The present local ring is not a nontrivial product and has embedding dimension three, unlike a chain ring.

Masalkar et al. give a general unit-equivalence partition and generalized join of complete or empty graphs. This anticipates the quotient method for the graph; applying it here still requires computing the unit classes and cross adjacencies. Their explicit semisimple calculations do not cover a nonzero radical. Rather's simple-graph spectra for a univariate truncation over Z_p use one generator for the maximal ideal.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General partitions and weighted quotients are applicable tools but require the ring-specific incidence and quotient evaluation. Neither the semisimple formulas nor the explicit univariate/chain-ring spectral results can be specialized to this ring.

evidence: The accessible Aliniaeifard–Li abstract addresses recognition of modular finite abelian p-group rank/order and isomorphism for semisimple group rings. Those stated implications do not construct the rank-three graph from its ring presentation. The frozen review reports fuller §2–3 inspection, but this was not independently reproduced.

Even with the general join theorem, to identify explicit unit classes one must compute how unit multiplication changes v,w,t; the image of multiplication by v in degree two is the kernel of the complementary pairing with v. This leads to the nontrivial normalized scalar s and the line-point blocks; quotient spectrum then requires NNᵀ on the centered subspaces.
The tensor quotient of the squarefree rigidity theorem classifies maps vanishing on already known zero products, not the incidence of the pairs themselves.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new statement is not a substitute parameter into an existing displayed spectral formula. The explicit classes, cross-edges and determinant supply independent work beyond general methodology or rank/degree recognition.

evidence: The commutative characteristic-two group ring, three-variable quadratic truncation, and characteristic-two three-generator exterior algebra are equivalent formulations of the ring. Recognizing the projective line directions in J₂ and the scalar fibers in directions of J₁ is additional structure, not another name for squarefreeness.

The nearby bivariate-cubic result concerns the square-zero induced graph of a nine-dimensional ring, with q⁵-1 vertices and one universal clique joined to q+1 cliques; the present ordinary graph has q⁷-1 vertices and nontrivial point–line incidence across the classes.
The squarefree-radical rigidity result uses the same truncation at r=3 but identifies multilinear tensor-span or bilinear-map quotients rather than the graph or eigenvalues.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Dualizing points and lines does not equate the compared same-algebra bilinear invariant or the other ring's two-stratum join with the claimed spectrum. The graph being ordinary rather than retaining square-zero loops is essential: retaining those loops adds I and shifts the eigenvalues.

originality.rationale: The group-ring graph, its compression/generalized joins and the incidence spectral identity are known concepts. The contribution is the concrete projective-plane and scalar-class identification for this local squarefree ring and the resulting complete ordinary (loopless) adjacency factorization and nonsingularity across q. The compared sources cover methods, different rings or a weaker invariant, not that classification. One close early same-class article remained unavailable in independent full text.
residual_risks: Same-class Aliniaeifard–Li full text was not independently accessible. An implicit prior decomposition in that or another modular group-algebra graph treatment remains possible.
A more specialized compressed-graph or finite geometry classification under different terminology may overlap. Searches and the finite q=2 computation are not priority certification.

value.rationale: The ordinary graph is a standard invariant of modular group rings and the three-generator case is where a point–line incidence geometry naturally appears in the zero-product constraints. Recovering that incidence and all real adjacency eigenvalues for every q, with no zero eigenvalue, gives useful exact structure unavailable from graph diameter or minimum degree. The proof treats an infinite family and is not a one-off small spectrum.
